People around here don't like Alex Jones very much - but he has set a fine example when it comes to flogging various third party merchandise, and a line of his own labelled products - to produce a revenue stream that fiances his operation, which is now considerable.

I mention this because I have operated several business, my last being the most successful. It is not easy, it is hard work, over and above the work being done in this place already. What it does give you is a flow of profits that can be directed into expanding and growing the site, money to hire dedicated staff, etc. Money to pay rent, servers, and keep the lights on - money to pay the owners a salary for their time.

This is how small outfits become large outfits without being enslaved to the likes of some billionaire or another. Profit equals freedom, it's as simple as that.

Now, for a place like this, I recommend building a free ads market place - to compete against similar areas on other social networks. A classified ads sort of deal. However, also sell premium placement ads for top listing, and label them as such. Dedicated vendors have no problem purchasing this type of advertising - indeed, they often prefer to do so. It sets them aside as a dedicated and established vendor, pursuing serious commercial activity. This adds to their legitimacy in the eyes of the consumer and actually promotes sales. Voat gains a stream of revenue that grows as the market grows - yet bandwidth is negligible - and besides administering the ads themselves, and the money, there is not a lot else to do. The main business transactions, shipping, receiving, etc, all occurs between vendors and customers anyway.

The goal is to set up thriving commercial activity hub. Later on, it becomes easy to introduce products with a Voat endorsement, T-shirts, etc... Voat doesn't have to make the shirts - the vendors do that - they just license the logo. Voat gets a cut. The servers are paid.

The point is, the vendors will build the hub for you, all they need is a box within which to do so. Voat operates the box, and enjoys revenue from multiple streams as a result. I've seen others do this very successfully.

This of course, does not prevent Voat from earning revenues from other means - I just see it as something that starts small with growth potential, that can be successfully managed as the site itself expands. Down the road, when Voat has a million or two users, a marketplace like this has serious financial power in it's own right - a place vendors will choose not to ignore.

Remember - Free Speech and Free Enterprise go hand in hand - indeed one of the most important reasons to have the first is so you can then have the second. This is what the enemies of Voat fear most of all - Voat becoming financially independent.
